Extract starting values for a latent profile fit

Source: R/accessors.R
starting_values.Rd

Returns a multilpa_start object, the starting-value list multilpa() accepts as start, taken from a fitted model or from any list that carries the parameter blocks. The blocks are validated when the list is built.

Usage

starting_values(
  x,
  covariance = c("auto", "drop", "keep"),
  what = c("all", "measurement")
)

Arguments

x

A fitted multilpa model, or a list carrying profile_probabilities, group_probabilities, and the measurement blocks the model uses: means with variances or covariances for continuous indicators, response_probabilities for categorical ones. An all-categorical model needs no Gaussian block. Other elements are ignored. A missing block raises latents_bad_start; a fit with a noise component raises latents_unsupported_noise.

covariance

"auto" (the default) keeps covariances when the object carries them, "drop" always returns the diagonal parameterization, and "keep" requires covariances and raises latents_bad_start when they are absent.

what

"all" (the default) returns the measurement and mixing blocks. "measurement" omits profile_probabilities and group_probabilities, which are sized for the model that produced them; use it with fixed in multilpa() for a staged fit that changes the number of group classes.

Value

An object of class multilpa_start: the list multilpa() accepts as start, with elements means, variances, profile_probabilities and group_probabilities. When covariances are returned, covariances replaces variances; when the object carries a categorical measurement model, response_probabilities is added. what = "measurement" drops profile_probabilities and group_probabilities. The Gaussian blocks are unnamed and indexed by position; as.data.frame() returns them as a labelled table. response_probabilities keeps each indicator's name and each block's category names, and multilpa() matches the blocks by these labels, so a fit whose categorical indicators or categories do not match raises latents_bad_start. The object can be passed directly as start.

See also

get_results() for the values as tidy tables.

Examples

set.seed(7)
example_data <- data.frame(
  school = rep(seq_len(12), each = 10),
  score_a = rnorm(120), score_b = rnorm(120)
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                  n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
starting_values(fit)
#> Starting values: 2 profile(s), 2 continuous indicator(s)
#> Residual covariance: diagonal
#> Categorical indicators: 0
#> Mixing blocks: 1 group class(es)
#> Pass this to multilpa(start = ) as it is.
as.data.frame(starting_values(fit))
#>   profile indicator        mean  variance standard_deviation
#> 1       1         1  0.31636979 0.7483074          0.8650476
#> 2       1         2 -0.05291982 0.9149785          0.9565451
#> 3       2         1 -1.11359585 0.1018727          0.3191750
#> 4       2         2  0.79091589 0.2857973          0.5346002
refit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                    n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 1,
                    start = starting_values(fit))
logLik(refit)
#> 'log Lik.' -323.0197 (df=9)
